fact.en: Biomolecules are complex organic molecules that form the basis of life and are required for growth, maintenance, and survival.
fact.tl: Ang biomolecules ay mga kumplikadong organic molecule na bumubuo sa batayan ng buhay at kailangan para sa paglaki, pagpapanatili, at kaligtasan.
fact.bis: Ang biomolecules kay mga komplikadong organic molecule nga nagporma sa basehan sa kinabuhi ug gikinahanglan alang sa pagtubo, pagmentinar, ug pagkaluwas.

cards.illustration: A living cell with glowing molecules inside, showing the complex organic molecules that make up life.

fact.en: The four major classes of biomolecules are carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, and nucleic acids.
fact.tl: Ang apat na pangunahing klase ng biomolecules ay carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, at nucleic acids.
fact.bis: Ang upat ka pangunang klase sa biomolecules mao ang carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, ug nucleic acids.

cards.illustration: Four labeled jars each containing a different biomolecule: a sugar cube, a piece of meat, a drop of oil, and a DNA helix.

fact.en:
Why are biomolecules called macromolecules?

Because they are large molecules composed of thousands of covalently connected atoms!
fact.tl:
Bakit tinatawag na macromolecules ang biomolecules?

Dahil ang mga ito ay malalaking molecule na binubuo ng libo-libong covalently connected atoms!
fact.bis:
Ngano gitawag ug macromolecules ang biomolecules?

Tungod kay kini mga dagkong molecule nga gilangkuban sa libo-libo ka covalently connected atoms!

cards.illustration: A giant chain of colorful atoms linked together, showing thousands of connected atoms forming a large molecule.

fact.en: The six most common elements in biomolecules are carbon, hydrogen, nitrogen, oxygen, phosphorus, and sulfur, remembered as CHNOPS.
fact.tl: Ang anim na pinakakaraniwang elemento sa biomolecules ay carbon, hydrogen, nitrogen, oxygen, phosphorus, at sulfur, na tinatawag na CHNOPS.
fact.bis: Ang unom ka labing kasagarang elemento sa biomolecules mao ang carbon, hydrogen, nitrogen, oxygen, phosphorus, ug sulfur, nga gitawag ug CHNOPS.

cards.illustration: Six colored spheres representing the six CHNOPS elements, each labeled with its chemical symbol, floating together.

fact.en: Carbohydrates contain carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen.
fact.tl: Ang carbohydrates ay naglalaman ng carbon, hydrogen, at oxygen.
fact.bis: Ang carbohydrates adunay carbon, hydrogen, ug oxygen.

cards.illustration: A simple sugar molecule with three different colored atoms representing carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen.

fact.en: Proteins contain carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, and sulfur.
fact.tl: Ang proteins ay naglalaman ng carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, at sulfur.
fact.bis: Ang proteins adunay carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, ug sulfur.

cards.illustration: A protein chain made of colored atoms, with five different colors representing the five elements.

fact.en: Lipids contain carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, phosphorus, and sulfur.
fact.tl: Ang lipids ay naglalaman ng carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, phosphorus, at sulfur.
fact.bis: Ang lipids adunay carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, phosphorus, ug sulfur.

cards.illustration: A fat molecule with five different colored atoms representing the five elements found in lipids.

fact.en: Nucleic acids contain carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, phosphorus, nitrogen, and sulfur.
fact.tl: Ang nucleic acids ay naglalaman ng carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, phosphorus, nitrogen, at sulfur.
fact.bis: Ang nucleic acids adunay carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, phosphorus, nitrogen, ug sulfur.

cards.illustration: A DNA helix with six different colored atoms representing the six elements found in nucleic acids.

fact.en:
What are carbohydrates commonly known as?

They are commonly known as sugars, and they are chemically polyhydroxy aldehydes or ketones!
fact.tl:
Ano ang karaniwang tawag sa carbohydrates?

Karaniwan silang tinatawag na sugars, at sila ay chemically polyhydroxy aldehydes o ketones!
fact.bis:
Unsa ang kasagarang tawag sa carbohydrates?

Kasagaran sila gitawag ug sugars, ug kini chemically polyhydroxy aldehydes o ketones!

cards.illustration: A spoonful of white sugar next to a honeycomb, showing sweet substances that are carbohydrates.

fact.en:
What is the difference between a monomer and a polymer?

A monomer is a single building unit, while a polymer is a long chain of many monomers linked together!
fact.tl:
Ano ang pagkakaiba ng monomer at polymer?

Ang monomer ay isang solong building unit, habang ang polymer ay mahabang kadena ng maraming monomer na magkakadugtong!
fact.bis:
Unsa ang kalainan sa monomer ug polymer?

Ang monomer kay usa ka building unit, samtang ang polymer kay taas nga kadena sa daghang monomer nga nagkadugtong!

cards.illustration: A single bead next to a long chain of identical beads, showing a monomer and a polymer.

fact.en: Carbohydrates are classified as monosaccharides, oligosaccharides, or polysaccharides based on the number of sugar units.
fact.tl: Ang carbohydrates ay inuuri bilang monosaccharides, oligosaccharides, o polysaccharides batay sa bilang ng sugar units.
fact.bis: Ang carbohydrates giklasipika isip monosaccharides, oligosaccharides, o polysaccharides base sa gidaghanon sa sugar units.

cards.illustration: Three groups of sugar cubes: one cube, a few cubes, and many cubes, representing the three classifications.

fact.en: Carbohydrates serve as an energy source, structural material such as cellulose, and stored energy forms like starch and glycogen.
fact.tl: Ang carbohydrates ay nagsisilbing source ng energy, structural material tulad ng cellulose, at stored energy forms tulad ng starch at glycogen.
fact.bis: Ang carbohydrates nagsilbi isip source sa energy, structural material sama sa cellulose, ug stored energy forms sama sa starch ug glycogen.

cards.illustration: A plant stem standing tall next to a potato and a piece of bread, showing structural and energy storage uses.

fact.en: Proteins are polymers of amino acids arranged in a chain called a polypeptide.
fact.tl: Ang proteins ay polymers ng amino acids na nakaayos sa isang kadena na tinatawag na polypeptide.
fact.bis: Ang proteins kay polymers sa amino acids nga gihan-ay sa usa ka kadena nga gitawag ug polypeptide.

cards.illustration: A chain of amino acid beads folding into a protein shape, showing the polypeptide chain.

fact.en:
What do proteins do in the body?

They help form hair, nails, and muscles, and they act as enzymes that speed up chemical reactions!
fact.tl:
Ano ang ginagawa ng proteins sa katawan?

Tumutulong sila sa pagbuo ng buhok, kuko, at muscles, at kumikilos sila bilang enzymes na nagpapabilis ng chemical reactions!
fact.bis:
Unsa ang gibuhat sa proteins sa lawas?

Motabang sila sa pagporma sa buhok, kuko, ug muscles, ug molihok sila isip enzymes nga nagpapaspas sa chemical reactions!

cards.illustration: A person flexing a muscle, with hair and nails visible, and a small enzyme molecule speeding up a reaction nearby.

fact.en:
Why don't lipids dissolve in water?

Because lipids are hydrophobic, meaning they do not dissolve in water!
fact.tl:
Bakit hindi natutunaw ang lipids sa tubig?

Dahil ang lipids ay hydrophobic, ibig sabihin hindi sila natutunaw sa tubig!
fact.bis:
Ngano dili matunaw ang lipids sa tubig?

Tungod kay ang lipids kay hydrophobic, nagpasabot nga dili sila matunaw sa tubig!

title.tl: Ang Lipids ay Hindi Natutunaw sa Tubig
title.bis: Ang Lipids Dili Matunaw sa Tubig

cards.illustration: Oil droplets floating on top of water in a glass, showing that lipids do not mix with water.

fact.en: Lipids store energy, form protective layers on skin, and some steroid hormones regulate cell activity.
fact.tl: Ang lipids ay nag-iimbak ng energy, bumubuo ng protective layers sa balat, at ang ilang steroid hormones ay kumokontrol sa cell activity.
fact.bis: Ang lipids magtipig ug energy, magporma ug protective layers sa panit, ug ang pipila ka steroid hormones mokontrol sa cell activity.

cards.illustration: A cross-section of skin showing a protective oily layer, with fat cells storing energy below.

fact.en:
What do nucleic acids do?

They are the main information-carrying molecules of the cell, directing protein synthesis and determining inherited characteristics!
fact.tl:
Ano ang ginagawa ng nucleic acids?

Sila ang pangunahing information-carrying molecules ng cell, na nagdidirekta ng protein synthesis at tumutukoy ng inherited characteristics!
fact.bis:
Unsa ang gibuhat sa nucleic acids?

Sila ang pangunang information-carrying molecules sa cell, nga nagdumala sa protein synthesis ug nagtino sa inherited characteristics!

title.tl: Ang Nucleic Acids ay Nagdadala ng Impormasyon
title.bis: Ang Nucleic Acids Nagdala ug Impormasyon

cards.illustration: A DNA helix inside a cell, with arrows showing information flowing from DNA to protein.

fact.en: The two main classes of nucleic acids are deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) and ribonucleic acid (RNA).
fact.tl: Ang dalawang pangunahing klase ng nucleic acids ay deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) at ribonucleic acid (RNA).
fact.bis: Ang duha ka pangunang klase sa nucleic acids mao ang deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) ug ribonucleic acid (RNA).

cards.illustration: Two side-by-side helices, one labeled DNA and one labeled RNA, showing their similar but distinct structures.

fact.en:
Why is DNA called the master blueprint for life?

Because DNA contains the information on what proteins will be created, and it constitutes the genetic material in all free-living organisms!
fact.tl:
Bakit tinatawag na master blueprint ng buhay ang DNA?

Dahil ang DNA ay naglalaman ng impormasyon kung anong proteins ang gagawin, at ito ang bumubuo ng genetic material sa lahat ng free-living organisms!
fact.bis:
Ngano gitawag ug master blueprint sa kinabuhi ang DNA?

Tungod kay ang DNA adunay impormasyon kung unsang proteins ang himuon, ug kini ang naglangkob sa genetic material sa tanang free-living organisms!

cards.illustration: A blueprint drawing of a living organism, with DNA helix as the master plan.

fact.en: RNA is responsible for creating proteins based on the information given by DNA.
fact.tl: Ang RNA ay responsable sa paggawa ng proteins batay sa impormasyon na ibinigay ng DNA.
fact.bis: Ang RNA maoy responsable sa paghimo ug proteins base sa impormasyon nga gihatag sa DNA.

title.tl: Ang RNA ay Gumagawa ng Proteins

cards.illustration: An RNA molecule reading a DNA template and assembling amino acids into a protein chain.

fact.en: Nucleic acids are polynucleotides, long chainlike molecules composed of nearly identical building blocks called nucleotides.
fact.tl: Ang nucleic acids ay polynucleotides, mahahabang chainlike molecules na binubuo ng halos magkakaparehong building blocks na tinatawag na nucleotides.
fact.bis: Ang nucleic acids kay polynucleotides, tag-as nga chainlike molecules nga gilangkuban sa halos parehas nga building blocks nga gitawag ug nucleotides.

cards.illustration: A long chain of nucleotide building blocks, each with a base, sugar, and phosphate group.

fact.en:
What does the word monomer mean?

It comes from Greek words monos meaning single and meros meaning part, so a monomer is a single building unit!
fact.tl:
Ano ang ibig sabihin ng salitang monomer?

Galing ito sa mga salitang Greek na monos na nangangahulugang single at meros na nangangahulugang part, kaya ang monomer ay isang solong building unit!
fact.bis:
Unsa ang buot ipasabot sa pulong monomer?

Gikan kini sa mga pulong Greek nga monos nga nagpasabot ug single ug meros nga nagpasabot ug part, busa ang monomer kay usa ka building unit!

cards.illustration: A single bead with the Greek letters monos and meros written beside it, showing the word origin.
